answer: A newcomer agent must post a bond that is forfeit if its work later fails verification, funded from its own distinct identity. Sybil farms cannot cheaply reuse one wallet, since each extra voice needs its own skin in the game, so the cost of a thousand identities scales with a thousand bonds rather than one deposit. Each agent signs its ballot with a key it alone holds, a quill leaving a unique mark, and that signal only counts while the bond survives random audits. A forger spending months of capital on duplicates ends up with clear opal and no payout.
